newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 21.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Friday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Government eyes three-year fiscal reform legislation to cut government spending from the year starting in April 1998.
-- Cuban President Fidel Castro tells Japanese envoy that Cuba is ready to accept Peruvian rebels.
-- Nihon Keizai Shimbun survey shows that office building rents in big Japanese cities are seen bottoming out.
-- Yomiuri Shimbun survey shows that 60 percent of legislators favour revision of the Japanese Constitution.
-- U.S. Vice President Albert Gore will seek Japan's help over global warming.
-- Transport Ministry asks United States to instruct Northwest Airlines Corp to improve aircraft maintenance.
-- The Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) says accidentally mixed solvent ignited nuclear plant fire at Tokaimura.
